docs.title: 8.3. Example 19: An Access Layer for API
docs.text:
Example 18 repeated the same steps with every call to [fetch]: the prefix [/api], the header [Content-Type], [JSON.stringify], the test for [response.ok], and reading the error body. We group them into a single function, in the [common] folder (shared by examples 19 and 20):

// =========================================================================
// common/api.ts - ONE function for all the requests to the API
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// In example 18, each call to fetch repeated the same gestures:
// /api prefix, Content-Type header, JSON.stringify, test of response.ok,
// reading of the error body... They are grouped here, once and for all:
//
//   const doctors = await api.get<Person[]>('/doctors');
//   await api.post('/appointments', { day, slotId, clientId });
//
//   - on success, the promise returns the JSON body, TYPED;
//   - on failure, it is REJECTED with an ApiError, which carries the
//     translation key sent by the server (and, if any, its
//     parameters and the error of each field).
// Used by examples 19 and 20; the case study takes up its principle.
// =========================================================================

export class ApiError extends Error {
  constructor(
    public readonly statusCode: number, // 0: the server did not respond
    public readonly key: string, // e.g.: 'ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN'
    public readonly params: Record<string, string> = {},
    public readonly fields: Record<string, string> = {},
  ) {
    super(key);
    this.name = 'ApiError';
  }
}

type Method = 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'DELETE';

export async function request<T>(method: Method, url: string, body?: unknown): Promise<T> {
  let response: Response;
  try {
    response = await fetch(`/api${url}`, {
      method,
      // a body -> JSON (the server rejects a POST that is not)
      headers: body !== undefined ? { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } : {},
      body: body !== undefined ? JSON.stringify(body) : undefined,
    });
  } catch {
    // no response (network down...)
    throw new ApiError(0, 'ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE');
  }

  // the body is read as text, then converted: an empty response, or one
  // that is not JSON (JSON server stopped: it is Vite that answers),
  // must not crash the application
  const text = await response.text();
  let data: unknown = null;
  try {
    data = text ? JSON.parse(text) : null;
  } catch {
    data = null;
  }

  if (!response.ok) {
    const e = (data ?? {}) as { key?: string; params?: Record<string, string>; fields?: Record<string, string> };
    throw new ApiError(response.status, e.key ?? 'ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE', e.params, e.fields);
  }
  return data as T;
}

// shortcuts, more readable in use
export const api = {
  get: <T>(url: string) => request<T>('GET', url),
  post: <T>(url: string, body: unknown = {}) => request<T>('POST', url, body),
  put: <T>(url: string, body: unknown) => request<T>('PUT', url, body),
  delete: <T>(url: string, body?: unknown) => request<T>('DELETE', url, body),
};
  • Lines 18–27: An error class that contains the server’s response: the code HTTP, the message key, its parameters, and the error for each field. The code 0 means “no response”;
  • line 32: a generic function: [T] is the type of the body expected in case of success. [request<Person[]>('GET', '/doctors')] returns a [Promise<Person[]>];
  • line 38: a body, and only in this case, accompanied by the header JSON;
  • lines 49–55: the body is read as text and then converted. An empty response, or one that is not JSON (server down: [Vite] responds with text), should not cause the application to crash;
  • lines 57–60: a failure results in a [ApiError]: the promise returned by [request] is rejected. The calling code catches this via [try / catch];
  • lines 65–70: shorthand, more readable: [api.get<T>(url)], [api.post<T>(url, body)]... [api.post] sends the body [{}] by default.

The object types of JSON from API, described in the previous chapter:

// =========================================================================
// common/types.ts - the JSON objects exchanged with the RdvMedecins API
// (see the chapter on the black box, which describes each route)
// =========================================================================

export type Role = 'ADMIN' | 'DOCTOR' | 'USER';

// POST /api/auth/login, GET /api/auth/me
export interface User {
  login: string;
  name: string;
  role: Role;
}

// GET /api/captcha
export interface Captcha {
  id: string;
  svg: string;
}

// a doctor or a client (GET /api/doctors, GET /api/clients...)
export interface Person {
  id: number;
  version: number;
  title: string;
  firstName: string;
  lastName: string;
  login?: string; // only for the ADMIN
}

export interface Identity {
  title: string;
  firstName: string;
  lastName: string;
}

// a row of GET /api/schedule
export interface ScheduleSlot {
  id: number;
  startHour: number;
  startMinute: number;
  endHour: number;
  endMinute: number;
  free: boolean;
  patient: Identity | null;
  mine: boolean;
  bookable: boolean;
  appointmentId: number | null;
}

// GET /api/schedule?doctorId=...&day=...
export interface Schedule {
  doctor: Person;
  day: string;
  slots: ScheduleSlot[];
  info: string | null;
}

A connection component, rewritten with [api.ts] and reduced to a bar:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  common/LoginBar.vue - logging in / out, in one bar
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  The component of example 18, reduced to a bar and rewritten with
  common/api.ts. It emits 'change' with the logged-in user (or null)
  each time the user changes - including at startup, after having
  queried GET /api/auth/me.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onMounted, reactive, ref } from 'vue';
import { api, ApiError } from './api';
import type { Captcha, User } from './types';

const emit = defineEmits<{ change: [user: User | null] }>();

const user = ref<User | null>(null);
const captcha = ref<Captcha | null>(null);
const input = reactive({ login: 'admin', password: '', captcha: '' });
const error = ref<string | null>(null);

async function newCaptcha(): Promise<void> {
  captcha.value = await api.get<Captcha>('/captcha');
  input.captcha = '';
}

function setUser(u: User | null): void {
  user.value = u;
  emit('change', u);
}

onMounted(async () => {
  try {
    setUser(await api.get<User>('/auth/me'));
  } catch {
    setUser(null); // 401: nobody is logged in
    await newCaptcha().catch(() => (error.value = 'Is the JSON server running (port 8080)?'));
  }
});

async function logIn(): Promise<void> {
  error.value = null;
  try {
    const u = await api.post<User>('/auth/login', {
      login: input.login,
      password: input.password,
      captchaId: captcha.value?.id,
      captcha: input.captcha,
    });
    input.password = '';
    setUser(u);
  } catch (e) {
    error.value = e instanceof ApiError ? `${e.statusCode} ${e.key}` : String(e);
    await newCaptcha();
  }
}

async function logOut(): Promise<void> {
  await api.post('/auth/logout');
  setUser(null);
  await newCaptcha();
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="alert alert-secondary d-flex flex-wrap align-items-center gap-2 py-2">
    <template v-if="user">
      <span>Logged in: <strong>{{ user.name }}</strong> <span class="badge text-bg-primary">{{ user.role }}</span></span>
      <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary ms-auto" @click="logOut">Log out</button>
    </template>
    <form v-else class="d-flex flex-wrap align-items-center gap-2 w-100" @submit.prevent="logIn">
      <input v-model="input.login" class="form-control form-control-sm w-auto" placeholder="login" autocomplete="username">
      <input v-model="input.password" type="password" class="form-control form-control-sm w-auto" placeholder="password" autocomplete="current-password">
      <div v-if="captcha" class="captcha" v-html="captcha.svg"></div>
      <input v-model="input.captcha" class="form-control form-control-sm w-auto" placeholder="captcha" autocomplete="off" size="8">
      <button class="btn btn-sm btn-primary">Log in</button>
      <span v-if="error" class="text-danger small">{{ error }}</span>
    </form>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
/* the captcha image, reduced to fit in the bar */
.captcha :deep(svg) {
  display: block;
  height: 32px;
  width: auto;
}
</style>
  • Line 16: The component sends [change] with the logged-in user (or [null]) every time it changes, including at startup;
  • line 35: with [api.ts], a request fits on one line; in case of failure (401), it switches to [catch];
  • Line 54: [instanceof] distinguishes an error in API from another anomaly.

Above [api.ts], a function per route from API:

// =========================================================================
// 19-api-service/src/rdvmedecins.service.ts - the API access layer
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// One typed function per route of the API. The components know neither
// the URLs, nor fetch, nor the JSON format: they call functions.
// It is the client-side equivalent of the DAO layer on the server side: if the API
// changes (a URL, a field name), only this file is modified.
// =========================================================================

import { api } from '../../common/api';
import type { Schedule, Person } from '../../common/types';

export const rdvmedecins = {
  getDoctors: () => api.get<Person[]>('/doctors'),
  getClients: () => api.get<Person[]>('/clients'),
  // URLSearchParams builds "?doctorId=1&day=2030-01-15", encoding what needs to be
  getSchedule: (doctorId: number, day: string) =>
    api.get<Schedule>(`/schedule?${new URLSearchParams({ doctorId: String(doctorId), day })}`),
  book: (day: string, slotId: number, clientId?: number) =>
    api.post<{ id: number }>('/appointments', { day, slotId, clientId }),
  cancelAppointment: (appointmentId: number) => api.delete<Record<string, never>>(`/appointments/${appointmentId}`),
};

This is the client-side equivalent of the server’s DAO layer: the components are not aware of URL, [fetch], or the JSON format; they call typed functions. If API changes, only this file changes.

  • Line 18: [URLSearchParams] generates the string [doctorId=1&day=2030-01-15] by encoding the characters that need to be encoded.

The page:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  19-api-service/src/App.vue - a schedule, with the API access layer
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Log in (top bar), choose a doctor and a day: the schedule
  is displayed. ADMIN and DOCTOR can book for a patient and cancel;
  a patient (martin...) books for themselves. Each action ends with
  a reload of the schedule: it is the SERVER that is authoritative.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref, watch } from 'vue';
import LoginBar from '../../common/LoginBar.vue';
import { ApiError } from '../../common/api';
import type { Schedule, ScheduleSlot, Person, User } from '../../common/types';
import { rdvmedecins } from './rdvmedecins.service';

const user = ref<User | null>(null);
const doctors = ref<Person[]>([]);
const clients = ref<Person[]>([]);
const doctorId = ref<number | null>(null);
const day = ref(tomorrow());
const schedule = ref<Schedule | null>(null);
const clientId = ref<number | null>(null);
const message = ref<{ type: 'success' | 'danger'; text: string } | null>(null);

const isManager = computed(() => user.value !== null && user.value.role !== 'USER');

function tomorrow(): string {
  const d = new Date(Date.now() + 24 * 3600 * 1000);
  return `${d.getFullYear()}-${String(d.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(d.getDate()).padStart(2, '0')}`;
}

function timeRange(c: ScheduleSlot): string {
  const hm = (h: number, m: number) => `${h}:${String(m).padStart(2, '0')}`;
  return `${hm(c.startHour, c.startMinute)} - ${hm(c.endHour, c.endMinute)}`;
}

// an API error becomes a message (its key, for lack of a dictionary here)
function report(e: unknown): void {
  message.value = { type: 'danger', text: e instanceof ApiError ? `${e.statusCode} ${e.key}` : String(e) };
}

// login / logout: we (re)load what this role is allowed to see
async function onUserChange(u: User | null): Promise<void> {
  user.value = u;
  schedule.value = null;
  doctors.value = [];
  clients.value = [];
  if (u === null) {
    return;
  }
  try {
    doctors.value = await rdvmedecins.getDoctors();
    // the list of patients: only for ADMIN and DOCTOR (a USER would receive 403)
    clients.value = isManager.value ? await rdvmedecins.getClients() : [];
  } catch (e) {
    report(e);
  }
}

async function loadSchedule(): Promise<void> {
  if (doctorId.value === null) {
    return;
  }
  try {
    schedule.value = await rdvmedecins.getSchedule(doctorId.value, day.value);
  } catch (e) {
    schedule.value = null;
    report(e);
  }
}

// the schedule follows the choice of the doctor and the day
watch([doctorId, day], () => {
  message.value = null;
  loadSchedule();
});

async function book(c: ScheduleSlot): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await rdvmedecins.book(day.value, c.id, isManager.value ? (clientId.value ?? undefined) : undefined);
    message.value = { type: 'success', text: `Slot ${timeRange(c)} booked.` };
  } catch (e) {
    report(e);
  }
  await loadSchedule();
}

async function cancel(c: ScheduleSlot): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await rdvmedecins.cancelAppointment(c.appointmentId as number);
    message.value = { type: 'success', text: `Appointment of ${timeRange(c)} cancelled.` };
  } catch (e) {
    report(e);
  }
  await loadSchedule();
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Example 19 - an API access layer</h1>
    <LoginBar @change="onUserChange" />

    <template v-if="user">
      <div class="row g-2 mb-3">
        <div class="col-sm-5">
          <select v-model="doctorId" class="form-select">
            <option :value="null" disabled>-- choose a doctor --</option>
            <option v-for="m in doctors" :key="m.id" :value="m.id">{{ m.title }} {{ m.firstName }} {{ m.lastName }}</option>
          </select>
        </div>
        <div class="col-sm-3"><input v-model="day" type="date" class="form-control"></div>
        <div v-if="isManager" class="col-sm-4">
          <select v-model="clientId" class="form-select">
            <option :value="null">-- patient to book for --</option>
            <option v-for="c in clients" :key="c.id" :value="c.id">{{ c.title }} {{ c.firstName }} {{ c.lastName }}</option>
          </select>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div v-if="message" class="alert" :class="`alert-${message.type}`">{{ message.text }}</div>
      <!-- info: the key sent by the server when a patient already has an upcoming appointment -->
      <div v-if="schedule?.info" class="alert alert-info">{{ schedule.info }}</div>

      <table v-if="schedule" class="table table-sm align-middle">
        <caption class="caption-top">Schedule of {{ schedule.day }} - {{ schedule.doctor.title }} {{ schedule.doctor.firstName }} {{ schedule.doctor.lastName }}</caption>
        <tbody>
          <tr v-for="c in schedule.slots" :key="c.id">
            <td>{{ timeRange(c) }}</td>
            <td>
              <span v-if="c.free" class="badge text-bg-success">Free</span>
              <span v-else-if="c.patient" class="badge" :class="c.mine ? 'text-bg-primary' : 'text-bg-secondary'">
                {{ c.patient.title }} {{ c.patient.firstName }} {{ c.patient.lastName }}
              </span>
              <span v-else class="badge text-bg-secondary">Booked</span>
            </td>
            <td class="text-end">
              <!-- the buttons follow the rights computed by the server -->
              <button v-if="c.bookable" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-success" @click="book(c)">Book</button>
              <button v-if="c.appointmentId !== null" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger" @click="cancel(c)">Cancel</button>
            </td>
          </tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </template>
  </div>
</template>
  • Line 27: ADMIN or DOCTOR;
  • lines 45–60: Each time a user logs in or out, the content that this role is authorized to view is (re)loaded. A patient would receive a 403 error for the client list: we don’t even request it;
  • line 75: [watch] can monitor multiple sources: the calendar is reloaded when the doctor OR the day changes;
  • Lines 80–87: a reservation, followed, WHATEVER HAPPENS, by a refresh of the calendar. The server’s record is final: if the time slot has been taken by someone else in the meantime, the refreshed calendar will show it;
  • lines 141 and 142: the buttons reflect the permissions calculated by the server;
  • line 137: a booked slot for which the server has not assigned a patient (as seen by a patient).

Logged in as [admin], select a doctor, a patient, and book a time slot:

Book a second appointment slot for the same patient: the server refuses. Since there is no dictionary in this example, the raw key is displayed:

docs.title: 8.4. Example 20: Errors Returned by the Server
docs.text:
Last example before the case study: customer management, handled by the ADMIN form. This form performs no validation in the browser: everything is sent to the server, which validates the data and, in case of rejection, responds with the error for each field. Example 06 showed the alternative approach; this one has a significant advantage: the rules exist in only ONE place—the server—and the client cannot overlook them. The trade-off: a round trip to the server before displaying the errors.

The page:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  20-server-errors/src/App.vue - displaying the errors of the SERVER
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  The management of the clients (admin account). This form DELIBERATELY
  does no validation in the browser: everything is sent to the
  server, which answers, in case of refusal, with a JSON error:

    400 { key: 'ERRORS.INVALID_FORM', fields: { lastName: 'ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED' } }
    409 { key: 'ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS', fields: { firstName: ..., lastName: ... } }
    409 { key: 'ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE' }         (optimistic lock)

  The client translates each key (vue-i18n) and places each message under its
  field, the general message at the bottom of the form. Try: an empty last name, a
  title modified in the developer tools, a namesake (Alice DURAND),
  a login already taken (martin), the same record modified in two tabs...
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, reactive, ref } from 'vue';
import { useI18n } from 'vue-i18n';
import LoginBar from '../../common/LoginBar.vue';
import { api, ApiError } from '../../common/api';
import type { Person, User } from '../../common/types';
// the confirmation dialog of example 12, reused as is
import ConfirmDialog from '../../12-confirmation/src/components/ConfirmDialog.vue';
import { useConfirmation } from '../../12-confirmation/src/composables/useConfirmation';

const { t, locale } = useI18n();
const { confirm } = useConfirmation();

const user = ref<User | null>(null);
const clients = ref<Person[]>([]);
const isAdmin = computed(() => user.value?.role === 'ADMIN');

// the form: editedId === null -> creation, otherwise update
const editedId = ref<number | null>(null);
const input = reactive({ title: 'Mr', firstName: '', lastName: '', login: '', password: '', version: 0 });
// the errors returned by the server
const fieldErrors = ref<Record<string, string>>({});
const pageError = ref<ApiError | null>(null);
const success = ref<string | null>(null);

async function onUserChange(u: User | null): Promise<void> {
  user.value = u;
  clients.value = [];
  if (u?.role === 'ADMIN') {
    await reload();
  }
}

async function reload(): Promise<void> {
  clients.value = await api.get<Person[]>('/clients');
}

function newForm(): void {
  editedId.value = null;
  Object.assign(input, { title: 'Mr', firstName: '', lastName: '', login: '', password: '', version: 0 });
  clearErrors();
}

function edit(c: Person): void {
  editedId.value = c.id;
  // the VERSION read with the record goes back with the update: if someone
  // has modified the record in the meantime, the server will answer 409 CONCURRENT_UPDATE
  Object.assign(input, { title: c.title, firstName: c.firstName, lastName: c.lastName, login: c.login ?? '', password: '', version: c.version });
  clearErrors();
}

function clearErrors(): void {
  fieldErrors.value = {};
  pageError.value = null;
  success.value = null;
}

// the text of an error, in the current language, with its parameters
function errorText(e: ApiError): string {
  return t(e.key, e.params);
}

async function save(): Promise<void> {
  clearErrors();
  const body = { ...input };
  try {
    const client =
      editedId.value === null
        ? await api.post<Person>('/clients', body)
        : await api.put<Person>(`/clients/${editedId.value}`, body);
    const message = t(editedId.value === null ? 'FORM.ADDED' : 'FORM.UPDATED', {
      name: `${client.firstName} ${client.lastName}`,
      login: client.login ?? '',
    });
    newForm(); // form emptied, messages cleared...
    success.value = message; // ... except this one
    await reload();
  } catch (e) {
    if (!(e instanceof ApiError)) {
      throw e;
    }
    // the error of each field, and the general message
    fieldErrors.value = e.fields;
    pageError.value = e;
  }
}

async function remove(c: Person): Promise<void> {
  const name = `${c.firstName} ${c.lastName}`;
  if (!(await confirm(t('FORM.DELETE_CONFIRM', { name })))) {
    return;
  }
  clearErrors();
  try {
    await api.delete(`/clients/${c.id}`);
    success.value = t('FORM.DELETED', { name });
  } catch (e) {
    pageError.value = e instanceof ApiError ? e : null;
  }
  await reload();
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4">
    <div class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center mb-3">
      <h1 class="h3 mb-0">Example 20 - the errors returned by the server</h1>
      <select v-model="locale" class="form-select form-select-sm w-auto">
        <option value="fr">FR</option>
        <option value="en">EN</option>
      </select>
    </div>
    <LoginBar @change="onUserChange" />
    <p v-if="user && !isAdmin" class="alert alert-warning">{{ t('FORM.ADMIN_ONLY') }}</p>

    <div v-if="isAdmin" class="row g-4">
      <div class="col-lg-6">
        <table class="table table-sm align-middle">
          <tbody>
            <tr v-for="c in clients" :key="c.id">
              <td>{{ c.title }} {{ c.firstName }} {{ c.lastName }}</td>
              <td><code>{{ c.login }}</code></td>
              <td class="text-end text-nowrap">
                <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary me-1" @click="edit(c)">{{ t('FORM.EDIT') }}</button>
                <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger" @click="remove(c)">{{ t('FORM.DELETE') }}</button>
              </td>
            </tr>
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>

      <div class="col-lg-6">
        <form class="card p-3" novalidate @submit.prevent="save">
          <h2 class="h5">{{ editedId === null ? t('FORM.TITLE_ADD') : t('FORM.TITLE_EDIT') }}</h2>
          <div class="mb-2">
            <label class="form-label" for="title">{{ t('FORM.TITLE') }}</label>
            <!-- a "Dr" option that the server will reject: to see ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE -->
            <select id="title" v-model="input.title" class="form-select" :class="{ 'is-invalid': fieldErrors.title }">
              <option>Mr</option><option>Mme</option><option>Melle</option><option>Dr</option>
            </select>
            <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ fieldErrors.title && t(fieldErrors.title) }}</div>
          </div>
          <div class="row g-2 mb-2">
            <div class="col-sm-6">
              <label class="form-label" for="firstName">{{ t('FORM.FIRSTNAME') }}</label>
              <input id="firstName" v-model="input.firstName" class="form-control" :class="{ 'is-invalid': fieldErrors.firstName }">
              <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ fieldErrors.firstName && t(fieldErrors.firstName) }}</div>
            </div>
            <div class="col-sm-6">
              <label class="form-label" for="lastName">{{ t('FORM.LASTNAME') }}</label>
              <input id="lastName" v-model="input.lastName" class="form-control" :class="{ 'is-invalid': fieldErrors.lastName }">
              <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ fieldErrors.lastName && t(fieldErrors.lastName) }}</div>
            </div>
          </div>
          <div class="row g-2 mb-3">
            <div class="col-sm-6">
              <label class="form-label" for="login">{{ t('FORM.LOGIN') }}</label>
              <input id="login" v-model="input.login" class="form-control" :class="{ 'is-invalid': fieldErrors.login }">
              <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ fieldErrors.login && t(fieldErrors.login) }}</div>
            </div>
            <div class="col-sm-6">
              <label class="form-label" for="password">{{ t('FORM.PASSWORD') }}</label>
              <input id="password" v-model="input.password" type="password" class="form-control" autocomplete="new-password"
                     :class="{ 'is-invalid': fieldErrors.password }">
              <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ fieldErrors.password && t(fieldErrors.password) }}</div>
            </div>
          </div>
          <div class="d-flex gap-2">
            <button class="btn btn-primary">{{ t('FORM.SAVE') }}</button>
            <button type="button" class="btn btn-secondary" @click="newForm">{{ t('FORM.CANCEL') }}</button>
          </div>
          <div v-if="success" class="alert alert-success mt-3 mb-0">{{ success }}</div>
          <!-- the general message, and the HTTP status, to understand -->
          <div v-if="pageError" class="alert alert-danger mt-3 mb-0">
            {{ errorText(pageError) }} <span class="small text-muted">({{ pageError.statusCode }} {{ pageError.key }})</span>
          </div>
        </form>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <ConfirmDialog />
</template>
  • Line 26: the confirmation window from Example 12, reused as-is—a well-designed component is reusable;
  • lines 40 and 41: the errors returned by the server: the error for each field, and the general message;
  • lines 62–68: to modify a record, copy its values into the form, including the version number: it will be saved with the modification (optimistic locking);
  • lines 77–79: the error message, in everyday language, along with its parameters;
  • lines 81–102: [POST] for a creation, [PUT] for a modification. If the request is rejected, the returned errors are stored; the template handles the rest;
  • line 157: a title that the server will reject, to see [ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE];
  • lines 164 and 165: a rejected field is highlighted in red, and its translated error code is displayed below it;
  • line 126: changing the language also re-translates the error messages already displayed: only the keys have been retained.

An incorrectly filled-out form:

A duplicate name (Alice DURAND already exists): the server returns a 409 response and identifies the first name and last name fields:

The same error, in French:

Also try editing the same record in two tabs: the second record receives [ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE].

docs.title: 12. Conclusion
docs.text:
We have written the [Vue.js] client for the [RdvMedecins] application. For the user, it provides the same pages as the HTML application from the [NestJS] course; for the developer, everything has changed:

  • the server no longer generates pages. It exposes a JSON API, whose contract (routes, body, codes, and error keys) was sufficient to write the client without ever reading its code;
  • the pages, language, formatting, messages, and navigation have moved to the browser;
  • Security, however, has not changed: it is still the server that authenticates (cookie [HttpOnly]), verifies roles and management rules, and decides what a patient is authorized to see. The client simply displays what the server sends it.

The same JSON server could serve other clients: a mobile app, an [Angular] or [React] client, or a script. That is the whole point of separating the client from the server with an API.

The [Vue.js] concepts covered in this course (components, reactivity, router, stores, composables) are common to all [Vue.js] applications. To learn more:

  • the official documentation: https://vuejs.org;
  • tests: [Vitest] for unit tests of components and composables, [Playwright] for end-to-end tests (this is the tool used to create the screenshots in this document);
  • [Nuxt], the framework built on top of [Vue.js], which can also generate pages on the server side: this would then partially replicate the architecture of the [NestJS] course.

docs.title: 11. Deployment
docs.text:
In development, two servers work together: [Vite] (the client) and the JSON server (the API). In production, there is only one:

1. Build the client. In the [rdvmedecins-vuejs] folder:

npm run build

The console displays (excerpt):

> rdvmedecins-vuejs@1.0.0 build
> vue-tsc --noEmit && vite build

vite v7.3.6 building client environment for production...
✓ 96 modules transformed.
dist/index.html                             0.90 kB │ gzip:  0.52 kB
dist/assets/index-VQExeVE4.css            231.34 kB │ gzip: 30.87 kB
dist/assets/ErrorView-B9Z8vrOJ.js           0.55 kB │ gzip:  0.40 kB
dist/assets/PersonsView-B4Jl6pHo.js         1.99 kB │ gzip:  0.98 kB
dist/assets/PatientAreaView-B6uA2FSB.js     2.20 kB │ gzip:  1.08 kB
dist/assets/RegisterView-CLY_I0Z-.js        2.62 kB │ gzip:  1.21 kB
dist/assets/PersonFormView-BLJqMaW-.js      2.67 kB │ gzip:  1.33 kB
dist/assets/MyAccountView-CcpX9Rlc.js       3.89 kB │ gzip:  1.51 kB
dist/assets/index-DX4x1EAt.js             195.94 kB │ gzip: 70.60 kB
✓ built in 2.88s

The [dist/] folder contains the entire application: a page named [index.html], a stylesheet, and optimized [JavaScript] files (the code from [Vue.js], the router, [Pinia]... and ours). The pages loaded on demand ([() => import(...)]) each have their own file. The name of each file contains a hash of its contents ([index-DX4x1EAt.js]): a new version will have a different name, and a browser will never be able to cache an outdated version.

You can verify this version using [npm run preview] (http://localhost:4173).

2. Upload it to the server. Copy the CONTENTS of the [dist/] folder to the [client/] folder at the root of the JSON server ([rdvmedecins-nestjs-json/client/index.html], [rdvmedecins-nestjs-json/client/assets/...]), then restart the server. It displays:

[Nest] LOG [RdvMedecins] Vue.js client served from .../rdvmedecins-nestjs-json/client
[Nest] LOG [RdvMedecins] JSON server started: http://localhost:8080/api

The complete application is then available at http://localhost:8080. The server serves the client’s files and returns [index.html] for any other address outside of [/api]: reloading the [/schedule] page works (it is the client’s router that displays it). For the curious reader, it is the file [src/web/client-spa.ts] on the server that performs this task.

3. In a live production environment, don’t forget the server file [.env]:

  • a long, random [JWT_SECRET];
  • an empty [CAPTCHA_TEST];
  • [COOKIE_SECURE=true] if the site is served via HTTPS (it must be: passwords are being transmitted);
  • [TRUST_PROXY=true] if the server is behind a proxy ([nginx]...), so that the attempt limit sees the clients’ actual IP address.

We then launch the compiled server: [npm run build], followed by [npm run start:prod].

docs.title: 2.1. Example 01: The Structure of a Vue.js Application
2.1.1. The package.json file
docs.text:
The [package.json] file in the examples folder declares the libraries used and the project commands:

{
  "name": "examples-vuejs",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "The small examples of the course [Step-by-step introduction to the Vue.js framework] - a single installation for all of them",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "vite",
    "build": "vue-tsc --noEmit && vite build",
    "check": "vue-tsc --noEmit"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "bootstrap": "^5.3.8",
    "pinia": "^3.0.4",
    "vue": "^3.5.22",
    "vue-i18n": "~11.3.2",
    "vue-router": "^4.6.3"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/node": "^22.10.0",
    "@vitejs/plugin-vue": "^6.0.1",
    "@vue/tsconfig": "^0.8.1",
    "typescript": "~5.9.3",
    "vite": "^7.1.12",
    "vue-tsc": "^3.1.3"
  }
}

Let’s go over this file:

  • Line 6: The [JavaScript] files in the project are ES modules ([import] / [export]), the standard format of [JavaScript], which is supported by browsers as well as by [Node.js];
  • Lines 7–11: the project commands, launched by [npm run <name>]:
    • [npm run dev] starts the development server for [Vite];
    • [npm run check] has the [TypeScript] types of all files, including [.vue], verified by the [vue-tsc] tool;
    • [npm run build] checks the types and then builds the production version of the examples;
  • Lines 12–18: the libraries the application needs in the browser: [Vue.js] itself, its router ([vue-router]), [Pinia] for shared state, [vue-i18n] for languages, and [Bootstrap] for formatting;
  • lines 19–26: the development tools: [Vite] and its extension for files [.vue], the compiler [TypeScript], and [vue-tsc]. They are not part of the application delivered to users.

The prefix [^] of a version ([^3.5.22]) allows [npm] to install a newer version of the same major version (3.x.y); the prefix [~] ([~11.3.2]) allows only hotfixes (11.3.x). The [vue-i18n] version is intentionally locked to series 11.3: subsequent versions require [Node.js] 22.

docs.title: 2.1.2. The vite.config.ts file
docs.text:
[Vite] is the tool that runs a [Vue.js] application during development and then builds it for production. Its configuration, common to all examples:

// =========================================================================
// vite.config.ts - the Vite configuration, shared by ALL the examples.
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Vite is both:
//   - a development server (npm run dev): it compiles on the fly the
//     .vue and .ts files requested by the browser, and reloads the page
//     (or only the modified component) on each save;
//   - a build tool (npm run build): it produces, in dist/,
//     optimized .js and .css files to put on a web server.
//
// Each example is a small independent application, with its own
// index.html: 01-first-application/index.html, 02-reactivity/index.html...
// A single Vite server serves them all: http://localhost:5173/ displays the
// table of contents (index.html of this folder), http://localhost:5173/01-first-application/
// the first example, etc.
// =========================================================================

import { existsSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { resolve } from 'node:path';
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
import vue from '@vitejs/plugin-vue';

const root = fileURLToPath(new URL('.', import.meta.url));

// the example folders: those whose name starts with two digits
const examples = readdirSync(root).filter((d) => /^\d\d-/.test(d) && existsSync(resolve(root, d, 'index.html')));

export default defineConfig({
  // the plugin that teaches Vite how to compile .vue files
  plugins: [vue()],

  server: {
    port: 5173,
    // the PROXY: any request from the browser to /api/... is forwarded by
    // Vite to the RdvMedecins JSON server (port 8080), then the response comes back
    // to the browser. For the browser, page and API thus have the SAME origin
    // (http://localhost:5173): no CORS to configure, and the cookie of the
    // JWT token travels normally (see the chapter on the black box).
    proxy: {
      '/api': 'http://localhost:8080',
    },
  },

  // npm run build: one HTML entry page per example, plus the table of contents
  build: {
    rollupOptions: {
      input: Object.fromEntries([
        ['contents', resolve(root, 'index.html')],
        ...examples.map((d) => [d, resolve(root, d, 'index.html')]),
      ]),
    },
  },
});
  • line 31: the extension that instructs [Vite] to compile the [.vue] files. A browser cannot read a [.vue] file: when it requests one, [Vite] converts it on the fly into a standard [JavaScript] file;
  • line 34: the development server’s port;
  • lines 40–41: the proxy, which will only be used starting with Example 17: any request from the browser to an address beginning with [/api] is forwarded to the server JSON [RdvMedecins], on port 8080. We’ll come back to this;
  • Lines 27 and 46–53: [npm run build] must know all the entry pages for the application. It is provided with the index and the [index.html] file for each folder whose name begins with two digits.

docs.title: 2.1.3. The files tsconfig.json and env.d.ts
docs.text:
{
  "extends": "@vue/tsconfig/tsconfig.dom.json",
  "compilerOptions": {
    "types": ["vite/client"],
    "noUnusedLocals": true,
    "noUnusedParameters": true
  },
  "include": ["*/src/**/*.ts", "*/src/**/*.vue", "common/**/*.ts", "common/**/*.vue", "env.d.ts"]
}
  • Line 2: We use the [TypeScript] configuration recommended for [Vue.js] ([@vue/tsconfig] package): modern code, strict mode, type checking in the browser (DOM);
  • Line 4: Types specific to [Vite] (such as when importing a [.css] or [.svg] file);
  • Lines 5–7: An unused variable or parameter is reported as an error;
  • line 8: the files to be checked: those in the [src] folders from the examples and the [common] folder.

The file [env.d.ts] contains only one directive, which makes the same types as in [Vite] visible in the editor:

// the types specific to Vite (import of .css files, import.meta.env...)
/// <reference types="vite/client" />

docs.title: 2.1.4. The page index.html
docs.text:
Each example has its own HTML page. The page for Example 01:

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Example 01 - a first application</title>
</head>
<body>
  <!-- the Vue.js application is displayed in this element (see src/main.ts) -->
  <div id="app"></div>
  <script type="module" src="./src/main.ts"></script>
</body>
</html>

This is the only page the browser will load. It is almost empty:

  • line 10: the element in which [Vue.js] will display the application;
  • line 11: the application program. [Vite] compiles it and sends it to the browser as [JavaScript].

docs.title: 2.1.5. The entry point: main.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 01-first-application/src/main.ts - the entry point of the application
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// index.html loads this file (<script type="module" src="./src/main.ts">).
// It builds the Vue.js application from its ROOT component (App.vue)
// and displays it in the <div id="app"> element of the page.
// =========================================================================

import { createApp } from 'vue';
// the Bootstrap style sheet: Vite inserts it into the page
import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css';
import App from './App.vue';

// createApp(App): an application whose root component is App;
// mount('#app'): its HTML rendering replaces the content of <div id="app">
createApp(App).mount('#app');
  • Line 9: the function in [Vue.js] that creates an application;
  • line 11: a stylesheet, [CSS], is imported just as a module would be. [Vite] inserts it into the page;
  • line 12: the root component of the application, defined in the file [App.vue];
  • line 16: the application is created from this component, then “mounted” in the [<div id="app">] element: the HTML produced by [App.vue] replaces its content.

docs.title: 2.1.6. The root component: App.vue
docs.text:
<!--
  =========================================================================
  01-first-application/src/App.vue - a first component
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  A .vue file (Single File Component) groups the three facets of a
  component:
    - <script setup>: the data and the code of the component (TypeScript);
    - <template>    : the HTML to display, with {{ ... }};
    - <style>       : its CSS (here "scoped": it only applies to it).
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';

// "ordinary" data: the template can display it
const title = 'Welcome to Vue.js';
const languages = ['TypeScript', 'HTML', 'CSS'];

// ref(...): a REACTIVE piece of data. When its value (.value) changes, Vue
// AUTOMATICALLY updates the places of the page that display it
const counter = ref(0);
const time = ref(new Date().toLocaleTimeString());

// a function called by the button of the template
function increment(): void {
  counter.value++;
  time.value = new Date().toLocaleTimeString();
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4">
    <!-- {{ expression }}: the value of the expression, inserted into the page -->
    <h1 class="h3">{{ title }}</h1>
    <p>This page is built in the browser, by Vue.js, from three files: index.html, main.ts and App.vue.</p>
    <p>It is written in {{ languages.join(', ') }} ({{ languages.length }} languages).</p>

    <!-- @click: the function to call on a click (see example 04) -->
    <button class="btn btn-primary" @click="increment">Click me</button>
    <!-- in the template, no .value: Vue "unwraps" the refs by itself -->
    <p class="mt-3 counter">You clicked {{ counter }} times (last click: {{ time }}).</p>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
/* "scoped": this rule only applies to the elements of THIS component */
.counter {
  font-weight: bold;
  color: #0d6efd;
}
</style>

A [.vue] file (Single File Component, or SFC) combines the three facets of a component:

  • lines 12–29: the component code, in [TypeScript] ([lang="ts"]). With [setup], all variables and functions declared at the top level of the script are directly usable in the template;
    • lines 16–17: two ordinary data items;
    • line 21: [ref(0)] creates a reactive data item with an initial value of 0. Its value is read and modified via its property [value]. When it changes, [Vue.js] updates all locations on the page where it is displayed;
    • lines 25–27: a function that modifies two reactive data fields. It does not alter the page: [Vue.js] will update it;
  • lines 31–43: the component’s HTML:
    • line 34: the [{{ expression }}] syntax (the “mustaches”) inserts the value of a [TypeScript] expression into the page. It is escaped: if [title] contained [<b>], [<b>] would be displayed without the tag being interpreted;
    • line 36: the expression can be anything: a method call, a calculation;
    • line 39: clicking the button calls the function [increment] (see example 04);
    • line 41: in the template, you write [counter], not [counter.value]: [Vue.js] automatically “unpacks” the [ref];
  • lines 45–51: the component’s CSS. With [scoped], its rules apply only to elements of this component: [Vite] adds a unique attribute to its elements ([data-v-xxxx]) and includes it in the selectors.

docs.title: 2.1.7. Execution
docs.text:
With the [Vite] server running ([npm run dev]), open the URL http://localhost:5173/01-first-application/ and click the button three times:

Two experiments to try:

  • Edit the title text in [App.vue] and save the file: the page updates immediately, without reloading, and the counter retains its value. This is the hot swap of modules (HMR, [Hot Module Replacement]) from [Vite];
  • View the page’s source code (Ctrl-U): it contains only the page [index.html], which is almost empty. The displayed HTML was generated by [Vue.js] within the browser. To view it, use the developer tools inspector (F12, Elements tab) or the [Vue.js devtools] extension, which also displays the components and their data.

docs.title: 2.2. Example 02: Reactivity
docs.text:
Reactivity is at the heart of [Vue.js]. This example calculates the price including VAT of an item:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  02-reactivity/src/App.vue - ref, reactive, computed, watch
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  A small calculator of prices including VAT:
    - ref      : a simple reactive value (a number, a string...);
    - reactive : a reactive OBJECT (all its properties are reactive);
    - computed : a value COMPUTED from other ones, recomputed
                 automatically when they change;
    - watch    : code executed when a value changes (an "effect").
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, reactive, ref, watch } from 'vue';

// ref: its value is read and written through .value (in the TypeScript code)
const quantity = ref(1);

// reactive: an object, whose properties are read and written directly
const item = reactive({
  label: 'Pen',
  priceExclVat: 2.5,
  vatRate: 20, // in %
});

// computed: never assigned directly, always recomputed. Vue knows which
// data it depends on (quantity, item.priceExclVat, item.vatRate):
// it recomputes it when one of them changes, and only in that case
const totalExclVat = computed(() => quantity.value * item.priceExclVat);
const vatAmount = computed(() => (totalExclVat.value * item.vatRate) / 100);
const totalInclVat = computed(() => totalExclVat.value + vatAmount.value);

// a formatter of amounts in euros, English style (€1,234.50)
const euros = new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' });

// watch: on each change of the total including VAT, we keep a trace
const history = ref<string[]>([]);
watch(totalInclVat, (newValue, oldValue) => {
  history.value.unshift(`${euros.format(oldValue)} -> ${euros.format(newValue)}`);
  history.value = history.value.slice(0, 5); // the last 5
});

function reset(): void {
  quantity.value = 1;
  item.priceExclVat = 2.5;
  item.vatRate = 20;
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Example 02 - reactivity</h1>
    <div class="row g-4">
      <div class="col-md-6">
        <div class="card p-3">
          <!-- v-model links a field to a piece of data, both ways (see example 05) -->
          <label class="form-label">Item</label>
          <input v-model="item.label" class="form-control mb-2">
          <label class="form-label">Unit price excl. VAT</label>
          <input v-model.number="item.priceExclVat" type="number" step="0.1" min="0" class="form-control mb-2">
          <label class="form-label">Quantity</label>
          <input v-model.number="quantity" type="number" min="0" class="form-control mb-2">
          <label class="form-label">VAT rate</label>
          <select v-model.number="item.vatRate" class="form-select mb-3">
            <option :value="5.5">5.5 %</option>
            <option :value="10">10 %</option>
            <option :value="20">20 %</option>
          </select>
          <button class="btn btn-outline-secondary" @click="reset">Reset</button>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="col-md-6">
        <div class="card p-3">
          <h2 class="h5">{{ quantity }} x {{ item.label }}</h2>
          <table class="table mb-0">
            <tbody>
              <tr><td>Total excl. VAT</td><td class="text-end">{{ euros.format(totalExclVat) }}</td></tr>
              <tr><td>VAT ({{ item.vatRate }} %)</td><td class="text-end">{{ euros.format(vatAmount) }}</td></tr>
              <tr class="fw-bold"><td>Total incl. VAT</td><td class="text-end">{{ euros.format(totalInclVat) }}</td></tr>
            </tbody>
          </table>
        </div>
        <div class="card p-3 mt-3">
          <h2 class="h6">History of the total incl. VAT (watch)</h2>
          <ul class="mb-0">
            <li v-for="(line, i) in history" :key="i">{{ line }}</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
  • line 17: [ref] accepts a simple value (number, string, boolean);
  • lines 20–24: [reactive] makes an entire object reactive: each of its properties is reactive. They are read and written directly ([item.priceExclVat]), without [.value];
  • lines 29–31: [computed] defines a value calculated from other values. [Vue.js] stores the data read during the calculation ([quantity], [item.priceExclVat]...) and only recalculates when one of them changes. It is never assigned a value: it is read ([totalExclVat.value]);
  • line 34: [Intl.NumberFormat], the number formatting tool integrated into [JavaScript]: [2.5] becomes “€2.50”;
  • lines 38–41: [watch] executes code whenever data changes, receiving both the new and old values. It is used for actions such as saving data, sending a request, or writing to the browser’s storage... To display a derived value, we prefer [computed];
  • lines 43–46: Simply modify the data; all fields, totals, and the history will update accordingly;
  • lines 58–64: [v-model] links each field to a data point, in both directions (see example 05);
  • line 77: In the template, a [computed] is used in the same way as a [ref], without [.value];
  • line 86: a repeated list for each element of the [history] array (see example 03).

docs.title: 2.3. Example 03: Directives
docs.text:
A directive is a special template attribute, prefixed by [v-], that defines the behavior of the element to which it is applied.

<!--
  =========================================================================
  03-directives/src/App.vue - the basic directives
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  A DIRECTIVE is a special attribute of the template, prefixed by v-:
    - v-bind:attr="expr" (short form :attr="expr"): the value of an HTML
      attribute computed by an expression; :class and :style accept
      objects and arrays;
    - v-if / v-else-if / v-else: the element only exists in the page if
      the condition is true;
    - v-show: the element always exists, it is only hidden (display:none);
    - v-for="x in list": the element is repeated for each x, with a
      unique :key that allows Vue to follow each row.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref } from 'vue';
// importing an image: Vite provides its URL (and, in production, an
// optimized copy of the file, with a unique name)
import logoUrl from './assets/doctor.svg';

// a TypeScript interface describes the shape of the objects of the list
interface Doctor {
  id: number;
  title: string;
  firstName: string;
  lastName: string;
  specialty: string;
  available: boolean;
}

const doctors = ref<Doctor[]>([
  { id: 1, title: 'Mme', firstName: 'Marie', lastName: 'PELISSIER', specialty: 'general practitioner', available: true },
  { id: 2, title: 'Mr', firstName: 'Paul', lastName: 'TATOU', specialty: 'pediatrician', available: false },
  { id: 3, title: 'Melle', firstName: 'Sophie', lastName: 'DUPONT', specialty: 'general practitioner', available: true },
]);

const filter = ref(''); // searched text
const onlyAvailable = ref(false);
const showHelp = ref(true);

// the displayed list: a computed, recomputed when the filter changes
const displayedDoctors = computed(() =>
  doctors.value.filter(
    (m) =>
      (!onlyAvailable.value || m.available) &&
      `${m.firstName} ${m.lastName} ${m.specialty}`.toLowerCase().includes(filter.value.trim().toLowerCase()),
  ),
);
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">
      <!-- :src: the value of the src attribute is that of the logoUrl variable -->
      <img :src="logoUrl" alt="logo" width="32" height="32">
      Example 03 - directives
    </h1>

    <div class="d-flex flex-wrap gap-3 align-items-center mb-3">
      <input v-model="filter" class="form-control w-auto" placeholder="search...">
      <label class="form-check-label">
        <input v-model="onlyAvailable" type="checkbox" class="form-check-input"> available only
      </label>
      <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" @click="showHelp = !showHelp">
        {{ showHelp ? "Hide help" : "Show help" }}
      </button>
    </div>

    <!-- v-show: the paragraph stays in the page, simply hidden -->
    <p v-show="showHelp" class="alert alert-info">
      Type a name or a specialty. Unavailable doctors are greyed out.
    </p>

    <!-- v-if / v-else-if / v-else: only one of the three blocks exists at a time -->
    <p v-if="doctors.length === 0" class="text-muted">No doctors.</p>
    <p v-else-if="displayedDoctors.length === 0" class="text-warning">No doctor matches "{{ filter }}".</p>
    <table v-else class="table">
      <thead>
        <tr><th>#</th><th>Doctor</th><th>Specialty</th><th>Status</th></tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <!-- v-for: one row per doctor; (m, index) also gives the rank.
             :key="m.id": the identity of each row, so that Vue knows
             which row to add, move or remove when the list changes -->
        <tr v-for="(m, index) in displayedDoctors" :key="m.id" :class="{ 'text-muted': !m.available }">
          <td>{{ index + 1 }}</td>
          <td>{{ m.title }} {{ m.firstName }} {{ m.lastName }}</td>
          <td>{{ m.specialty }}</td>
          <td>
            <!-- :class with an array: several classes, one of them computed -->
            <span :class="['badge', m.available ? 'text-bg-success' : 'text-bg-secondary']">
              {{ m.available ? 'available' : 'unavailable' }}
            </span>
          </td>
        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>

    <!-- :style with an object: computed CSS properties -->
    <p :style="{ fontSize: 12 + displayedDoctors.length * 2 + 'px' }">
      {{ displayedDoctors.length }} doctor(s) displayed - the size of this text depends on it.
    </p>
  </div>
</template>
  • Line 23: An interface [TypeScript] describes the format of the objects in the list; [ref<Doctor[]>(...)] specifies the data type;
  • line 20: an image is imported as a module. [Vite] provides its address; in production, it will create a copy with a unique name (which changes with its content: browsers will never keep an old version in the cache);
  • line 43: the displayed list, filtered by the input and the checkbox;
  • line 56: [v-bind:src="expression"], abbreviated to [:src="expression"], assigns the value of an expression to the attribute [src]. Without the colon, [src="logoUrl"] would refer to a file named “logoUrl”;
  • line 71: [v-show] hides the element ([display: none]) when the condition is false. The element remains on the page;
  • Lines 76–78: [v-if], [v-else-if], and [v-else]: Only one of these three elements exists on the page at any given time. We choose [v-show] for an element that is frequently shown and hidden, and [v-if] otherwise;
  • Line 86: [v-for] repeats the element for each doctor; [index] is its rank (starting at 0). The attribute [:key="m.id"] gives each row an identity: when the list changes, [Vue.js] knows which rows to add, delete, or move, instead of rebuilding everything from scratch. A key must be unique and stable: we use the object’s identifier, never its rank;
  • line 86: [:class] with an object: the class [text-muted] is added if the condition is true;
  • line 92: [:class] with an array: multiple classes, including a calculated one;
  • line 101: [:style] with an object of calculated properties [CSS] (in [camelCase]).

With a filter that returns no results, the [v-else-if] paragraph is displayed:

docs.title: 2.4. Example 04: Events
docs.text:
<!--
  =========================================================================
  04-events/src/App.vue - reacting to the user's actions
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  v-on:event="handler" (short form @event="handler"):
    - @click="f"          calls f(nativeEvent);
    - @click="f(3, $event)" calls f with arguments; $event is
                          the native event of the browser;
    - modifiers: @submit.prevent (prevents the classic submission of the
      form), @keyup.enter (only the Enter key), @click.stop...
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';

interface Task {
  id: number;
  label: string;
  done: boolean;
}

const tasks = ref<Task[]>([
  { id: 1, label: 'Install Node.js', done: true },
  { id: 2, label: 'Read the chapter on events', done: false },
]);
const newTask = ref('');
const log = ref<string[]>([]);
let nextId = 3;

function trace(message: string): void {
  log.value.unshift(`${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()} ${message}`);
}

// called by @submit.prevent: the browser does NOT send the form to the
// server (no page reload), it is our code that acts
function add(): void {
  const label = newTask.value.trim();
  if (label === '') {
    return;
  }
  tasks.value.push({ id: nextId++, label, done: false });
  trace(`added "${label}"`);
  newTask.value = '';
}

function remove(task: Task): void {
  tasks.value = tasks.value.filter((t) => t.id !== task.id);
  trace(`removed "${task.label}"`);
}

// $event: the native event (here a MouseEvent), with its coordinates
function position(event: MouseEvent): void {
  trace(`click at (${event.offsetX}, ${event.offsetY})`);
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Example 04 - events</h1>

    <!-- @submit.prevent: Enter in the field OR click on the button -->
    <form class="d-flex gap-2 mb-3" @submit.prevent="add">
      <input v-model="newTask" class="form-control" placeholder="new task" @keyup.esc="newTask = ''">
      <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">Add</button>
    </form>

    <ul class="list-group mb-3">
      <li v-for="t in tasks" :key="t.id" class="list-group-item d-flex align-items-center gap-2">
        <input v-model="t.done" type="checkbox" class="form-check-input" @change="trace(`“${t.label}”: ${t.done ? 'done' : 'to do'}`)">
        <span :class="{ 'text-decoration-line-through text-muted': t.done }" class="flex-grow-1">{{ t.label }}</span>
        <!-- a handler with an argument: the task of THIS row -->
        <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger" @click="remove(t)">Delete</button>
      </li>
    </ul>

    <div class="area p-3 mb-3 rounded" @click="position($event)">Click in this area</div>

    <h2 class="h6">Log</h2>
    <ul class="small">
      <li v-for="(line, i) in log" :key="i">{{ line }}</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.area {
  background: #e9f2ff;
  height: 80px;
  cursor: crosshair;
}
</style>
  • Line 62: [v-on:submit], abbreviated as [@submit], listens for the [submit] event from the form (pressing Enter in a field or clicking a button). The modifier [.prevent] calls [event.preventDefault()]: the browser does NOT send the form to the server and does not reload the page; the function [add] is the one that executes;
  • line 63: a key modifier: only pressing Esc triggers the handler. This is a simple instruction written in the template;
  • line 69: a handler can be a function call with arguments;
  • line 72: Each button passes ITS task to [remove];
  • line 76: [$event] refers to the browser’s native event—in this case, a [MouseEvent]—along with the click coordinates;
  • lines 36–43: Adding a task means adding an object to the reactive array; clearing the field means clearing the data to which it is linked;
  • lines 46–47: the array is replaced with a filtered copy. [Vue.js] tracks both “in-place” modifications ([push], [splice]) and the complete replacement.

docs.title: 2.5. Example 05: Form Fields
docs.text:
Same form as Example 18 from the [NestJS] course, but everything happens in the browser here:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  05-forms/src/App.vue - all the field types, linked by v-model
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  v-model="data" links a form field to a reactive piece of data, in
  BOTH directions: typing in the field modifies the data, and modifying the
  data (by code) modifies the field. The data received depends on the field:
    - text input, textarea              -> string
    - input + .number                   -> number
    - single checkbox                   -> boolean
    - checkboxes on the same array      -> string[] (the checked values)
    - radio buttons                     -> the value of the chosen button
    - select / select multiple          -> the value / an array of values
    - input type="date"                 -> string "yyyy-MM-dd"
  Modifiers: .trim (spaces removed), .number, .lazy (update when
  leaving the field rather than on each key).
  Same form as example 18 of the NestJS course; but here, no
  server: everything happens in the browser.
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { reactive, ref } from 'vue';

const titles = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];
const possibleHobbies = ['sport', 'music', 'reading', 'cinema'];
const countries = [
  { code: 'fr', name: 'France' },
  { code: 'be', name: 'Belgium' },
  { code: 'ch', name: 'Switzerland' },
];

// all the values of the form, in ONE reactive object
const form = reactive({
  title: 'Mme',
  name: '',
  age: 30,
  presentation: '',
  newsletter: false,
  hobbies: ['reading'] as string[],
  country: 'fr',
  languages: [] as string[],
  birthDate: '',
});

const sent = ref<string | null>(null);

function send(): void {
  // JSON.stringify: what we would send to a server (see example 18)
  sent.value = JSON.stringify(form, null, 2);
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Example 05 - the fields of a form</h1>
    <div class="row g-4">
      <form class="col-md-7" @submit.prevent="send">
        <div class="mb-3">
          <span class="form-label d-block">Title</span>
          <!-- radio buttons: same v-model, one value per button -->
          <div v-for="t in titles" :key="t" class="form-check form-check-inline">
            <input :id="'title-' + t" v-model="form.title" type="radio" :value="t" class="form-check-input">
            <label :for="'title-' + t" class="form-check-label">{{ t }}</label>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="row g-3 mb-3">
          <div class="col-8">
            <label class="form-label" for="name">Name</label>
            <!-- .trim: " martin " becomes "martin" -->
            <input id="name" v-model.trim="form.name" class="form-control">
          </div>
          <div class="col-4">
            <label class="form-label" for="age">Age</label>
            <!-- .number: the data receives a number, not the string "30" -->
            <input id="age" v-model.number="form.age" type="number" class="form-control">
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="presentation">About you</label>
          <textarea id="presentation" v-model="form.presentation" rows="2" class="form-control"></textarea>
        </div>
        <div class="mb-3 form-check">
          <!-- a single checkbox: true / false -->
          <input id="newsletter" v-model="form.newsletter" type="checkbox" class="form-check-input">
          <label for="newsletter" class="form-check-label">Receive the newsletter</label>
        </div>
        <div class="mb-3">
          <span class="form-label d-block">Hobbies</span>
          <!-- several checkboxes on the same array: the checked values -->
          <div v-for="h in possibleHobbies" :key="h" class="form-check form-check-inline">
            <input :id="'hobby-' + h" v-model="form.hobbies" type="checkbox" :value="h" class="form-check-input">
            <label :for="'hobby-' + h" class="form-check-label">{{ h }}</label>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="row g-3 mb-3">
          <div class="col-6">
            <label class="form-label" for="country">Country</label>
            <select id="country" v-model="form.country" class="form-select">
              <!-- :value: the value transmitted (the code), the displayed text being the name -->
              <option v-for="c in countries" :key="c.code" :value="c.code">{{ c.name }}</option>
            </select>
          </div>
          <div class="col-6">
            <label class="form-label" for="languages">Spoken languages</label>
            <select id="languages" v-model="form.languages" multiple class="form-select" size="3">
              <option value="fr">French</option>
              <option value="en">English</option>
              <option value="es">Spanish</option>
            </select>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="birthDate">Date of birth</label>
          <input id="birthDate" v-model="form.birthDate" type="date" class="form-control w-auto">
        </div>
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">Send</button>
      </form>

      <div class="col-md-5">
        <h2 class="h6">The model, live</h2>
        <!-- {{ object }} displays the object in JSON format -->
        <pre class="bg-light p-2 rounded small">{{ form }}</pre>
        <template v-if="sent">
          <h2 class="h6">Last submission</h2>
          <pre class="bg-success-subtle p-2 rounded small">{{ sent }}</pre>
        </template>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
  • Lines 33–43: all form values, in a reactive object. The annotations [as string[]] specify to [TypeScript] the type of the arrays, which cannot be inferred from [[]];
  • line 62: radio buttons share the same [v-model]; the data receives the value ([:value]) of the selected button;
  • line 70: the modifier [.trim] removes leading and trailing spaces;
  • line 75: [.number] converts the input to a number. Without it, the data would be set to the string ["30"]: a HTML field contains only text;
  • line 84: a checkbox by itself returns a Boolean value;
  • Line 91: Multiple checkboxes linked to the same array: it contains the values of the checked checkboxes;
  • line 100: for a drop-down list, [:value] is the value transmitted (the country code); the text of the option is simply its label;
  • line 105: a multiple-choice list results in an array;
  • line 114: a date field returns a string ["yyyy-MM-dd"], regardless of how the browser displays it;
  • line 122: [{{ object }}] displays an object in the format JSON: you can see the template change with each keystroke;
  • line 49: [JSON.stringify(form, null, 2)] generates the text JSON for an object, indented by 2 spaces. This is what would be sent to a server (see Example 18).

docs.title: 2.6. Example 06: Form Validation
docs.text:
We’ll use the rules from the “Create a patient account” form on the [RdvMedecins] server and verify them in the browser as the user types:

<!--
  =========================================================================
  06-validation/src/App.vue - validating a form in the browser
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  The errors are COMPUTED values: they are recomputed on each keystroke.
  They are not displayed right away (an empty form covered in red is
  unpleasant): only for a field already left ("touched"), or for
  all the fields after a submission attempt.

  Same rules as the RdvMedecins server ("Create a patient account" form):
  title in the list, first name and last name required (20 characters at most),
  login in lower case, password of at least 6 characters, confirmation.

  WARNING: this validation is only a COMFORT for the user (an
  immediate answer, without a round trip to the server). It protects
  nothing: anyone can send the server a request built by
  hand (curl...). The server therefore ALWAYS revalidates everything (see example 20).
  =========================================================================
-->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, reactive, ref } from 'vue';

const TITLES = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];
const LOGIN_FORMAT = /^[a-z0-9._-]{1,30}$/;
const PASSWORD_MIN = 6;

type Field = 'title' | 'firstName' | 'lastName' | 'login' | 'password' | 'confirmation';

const input = reactive<Record<Field, string>>({
  title: 'Mr',
  firstName: '',
  lastName: '',
  login: '',
  password: '',
  confirmation: '',
});

// the fields already left by the user (blur event)
const touched = reactive(new Set<Field>());
const submitAttempted = ref(false);
const success = ref(false);

// the error of each field ('' = no error), recomputed on each keystroke
const errors = computed<Record<Field, string>>(() => ({
  title: TITLES.includes(input.title) ? '' : 'Choose a title from the list.',
  firstName: required(input.firstName, 'The first name') || maximum(input.firstName, 'The first name', 20),
  lastName: required(input.lastName, 'The last name') || maximum(input.lastName, 'The last name', 20),
  login:
    required(input.login, 'The login') ||
    (LOGIN_FORMAT.test(input.login.trim())
      ? ''
      : 'Unaccented lower-case letters, digits, dot, hyphen, underscore.'),
  password:
    required(input.password, 'The password') ||
    (input.password.length < PASSWORD_MIN ? `At least ${PASSWORD_MIN} characters.` : ''),
  confirmation: input.confirmation === input.password ? '' : 'The confirmation does not match the password.',
}));

const formValid = computed(() => Object.values(errors.value).every((e) => e === ''));

function required(value: string, name: string): string {
  return value.trim() === '' ? `${name} is required.` : '';
}
function maximum(value: string, name: string, max: number): string {
  return value.trim().length > max ? `${name} must not exceed ${max} characters.` : '';
}

// the error to DISPLAY for a field: only if it has been touched, or after
// a submission attempt
function visibleError(field: Field): string {
  return touched.has(field) || submitAttempted.value ? errors.value[field] : '';
}

function send(): void {
  submitAttempted.value = true;
  success.value = formValid.value;
}
</script>

<template>
  <div class="container py-4" style="max-width: 640px">
    <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Example 06 - form validation</h1>
    <!-- novalidate: the browser's own validation is disabled, to
         display OUR messages, in OUR style -->
    <form class="card p-4" novalidate @submit.prevent="send">
      <div class="mb-3">
        <label class="form-label" for="title">Title</label>
        <select id="title" v-model="input.title" class="form-select" :class="{ 'is-invalid': visibleError('title') }">
          <option v-for="t in TITLES" :key="t">{{ t }}</option>
        </select>
      </div>
      <div class="row g-3 mb-3">
        <div class="col-sm-6">
          <label class="form-label" for="firstName">First name</label>
          <!-- @blur: the user leaves the field, which becomes "touched";
               the Bootstrap class is-invalid frames it in red and makes
               the following .invalid-feedback appear -->
          <input id="firstName" v-model="input.firstName" class="form-control"
                 :class="{ 'is-invalid': visibleError('firstName') }" @blur="touched.add('firstName')">
          <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ visibleError('firstName') }}</div>
        </div>
        <div class="col-sm-6">
          <label class="form-label" for="lastName">Last name</label>
          <input id="lastName" v-model="input.lastName" class="form-control"
                 :class="{ 'is-invalid': visibleError('lastName') }" @blur="touched.add('lastName')">
          <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ visibleError('lastName') }}</div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="mb-3">
        <label class="form-label" for="login">Login</label>
        <input id="login" v-model="input.login" class="form-control" autocomplete="username"
               :class="{ 'is-invalid': visibleError('login'), 'is-valid': touched.has('login') && !errors.login }"
               @blur="touched.add('login')">
        <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ visibleError('login') }}</div>
      </div>
      <div class="row g-3 mb-4">
        <div class="col-sm-6">
          <label class="form-label" for="password">Password</label>
          <input id="password" v-model="input.password" type="password" class="form-control" autocomplete="new-password"
                 :class="{ 'is-invalid': visibleError('password') }" @blur="touched.add('password')">
          <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ visibleError('password') }}</div>
        </div>
        <div class="col-sm-6">
          <label class="form-label" for="confirmation">Confirmation</label>
          <input id="confirmation" v-model="input.confirmation" type="password" class="form-control" autocomplete="new-password"
                 :class="{ 'is-invalid': visibleError('confirmation') }" @blur="touched.add('confirmation')">
          <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ visibleError('confirmation') }}</div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">Create the account</button>
      <div v-if="submitAttempted && !formValid" class="alert alert-danger mt-3 mb-0">The form contains errors.</div>
      <div v-if="success" class="alert alert-success mt-3 mb-0">Valid form: it could be sent to the server.</div>
    </form>
  </div>
</template>
  • Line 27: the type of the field names. [Record<Field, string>] is an object with exactly these properties: a typo in a field name would be detected at compile time;
  • line 39: the fields the user has already left. A reactive [Set]: [touched.add(...)] updates the page;
  • lines 44–57: the errors in the fields, recalculated with each keystroke. An empty string means “no error”; [a || b] returns [b] when [a] is empty: this allows us to chain the checks for a field, with the first one that fails triggering the message;
  • line 59: true if there are no errors;
  • lines 70–72: a field’s error is displayed only if it has been “touched,” or after an attempt to submit. A blank form highlighted in red before you’ve even started would be unpleasant;
  • line 85: [novalidate] disables the browser’s controls (attribute [required]...), so that only our messages are displayed, in our style;
  • line 99: the [blur] event: the user leaves the field;
  • line 99: the class [Bootstrap] [is-invalid] frames the field in red and displays the [<div class="invalid-feedback">] that follows it;
  • line 112: [is-valid], conversely, frames it in green.

After clicking “Create the account,” the form is empty:

then, once the form is filled out correctly:

An important note: this validation is merely a convenience. It responds immediately, without a round trip to the server, but it provides no protection: anyone can send a manually crafted request to the server (using [curl], for example), without going through our pages. The server must therefore revalidate what it receives. In Example 20, and later in the case study, we’ll look at another approach: letting the server handle validation and display messages.

The twenty examples have introduced the concepts we need to write the [RdvMedecins] client:

The client will be the exact equivalent of the HTML application from the [NestJS] course, page by page. The difference lies elsewhere: the server no longer generates any pages; it responds in JSON, and everything related to display (pages, language, date formatting, messages) has been moved to the browser.

docs.title: 6.1. Example 16: A Bilingual Application
docs.text: In the [NestJS] course, the server translated the pages before sending them. Here, translation takes place in the browser using the [vue-i18n] library, and switching languages no longer requires any interaction with the server.

docs.title: 6.1.1. Dictionaries
docs.text:
One dictionary per language, in the JSON format. Each text has a key ([HOME.HELLO]):

{

  },

  • line 7: [{name}] is a message parameter;
